To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure of CdnL from Thermus thermophilis has been determined and the results are presented in this manuscript.
The N-terminal domain of CdnL from the bacterium Thermus thermophilis is a compact, well-ordered protein with a novel three-helix fold that is likely to mediate protein–protein interactions.
the N-terminal domain of CdnL from T. thermophilus (CdnL-TthN) adopts an unusual fold that is similar to the N-terminal domain from the TRCF protein of T. thermophilis (TtrCFN).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of the CdnL protein family and the interactions of CdnL with RNAP-b, CarD, and TRCF.
the structural and functional characterization of the CarD-CdnL-TRCF protein family, and with the elucidation of the molecular details of its interactions with RNAP.
understanding the molecular details of interactions between the CarD_CdonL_TRCF protein domain family and RNAP-b.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CdnL protein family is a large group of proteins with a variety of functions that are still being discovered and characterized.
the N-terminal domain of the CdnL protein family is structurally similar to the N-terminal domain in the transcriptional regulator CarD.
the structure of CdnL has not been determined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is a very interesting protein that is conserved in bacteria, but its function has not been fully characterized.

we have obtained the NMR structure of a bacterial CdnL protein and have shown that it interacts with the same RNPA-b domain that CarD and TRCF also interact with, and that the CdnL protein has the same fold as the N-terminal domain of the CarD protein.

the N-terminal domain of CdnL (CdnLN) is a small protein that folds into an all-helical structure, with the first two helices (H1, H2) being connected by a flexible linker to the remaining four helices (H3–H6).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CarD_CDNL_TRCF protein fold is a novel one.

the N-terminal domains of CdnL, CarD and TRCF have a common structural core, and the structural basis for the functional differences among these proteins is likely to reside in their C-terminal domains.

the CdnL N-terminal domain (residues 1–180) is a well-folded, globular, monomeric protein that adopts the same overall structure regardless of whether it is expressed in E. coli or T. thermophilus, and regardless of whether or not it is fused to a C-terminal His tag.
